newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - OTC Bund vols firm, volumes at a trickle.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - OTC Bund vols firm, volumes at a trickle.

text.p: Trade in over-the-counter debt options was down to a trickle on Monday despite the recent hectic conditions in the underlying markets, with the only notable feature being a rise in Bund price volatility.
End users were few and far between, dealers said.
"They've all packed up for Christmas," said a dealer at a London house. "There's very little going on. Just position covering."
Robert Coughlan, options specialist at Paribas Capital Markets in London, said yo-yoing price action in the Bund market had pushed up cash vols but even here liquidity was thin.
Three-month price volatility on 10-year Bunds had risen to around six percent from as low as five percent a few weeks ago.
"It's based on illiquid Bund squeezes as opposed to anythning in the OTC market," Coughlan said.
He said most end-users had already squared up positions for their year-end accounting. "They'd effectively packed up and gone on their holidays by the start of December," he said.
Friday's news that European leaders had agreed on a pact to enforce fiscal discipline under monetary union, while weighing on the mark, was having little effect on the options market, traders said.
Coughlan said heavy mark-denominated supply in the early part of 1997 was more significant.
"We'll see a flood of paper hitting the market in the first two months of 1997. That will have a bigger impact than the euro pact that's just been agreed," he said.
